title: Right shifts of the specified completed integral tensor product
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi$, and put $A_n=R/\varpi^n$ for $n\geq1$. Let $W$ be a scheme on which $\ell$ is invertible. Use the small pro-etale site and the completed coefficient sheaf $B=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,W}=\varprojlim_n(A_n)_W$ of [def-pur-integral-derived-operations]. For objects $M,N$ of the ambient derived category $D(W_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)=D(B)$ of $B$-module sheaves, use the completed tensor $\widehat\otimes^L_R$ constructed in [def-pur-integral-derived-operations] by the functorial complex $\operatorname{Cone}(1-s)[-1]$ of the finite-reduction tensor tower, with the total tensor convention of [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. For each integer $r$ there is an isomorphism, natural in $M,N$,
$$
\sigma^r_{M,N}:M\widehat\otimes^L_R(N[r])\xrightarrow{\sim}(M\widehat\otimes^L_RN)[r].
$$
Here $C[r]^j=C^{j+r}$ and $d_{C[r]}=(-1)^r d_C$. The isomorphism is independent of the chosen flat-term K-flat resolutions. On such resolutions $P,Q$, its finite-level tensor comparison sends the summand $P_n^i\otimes Q_n^{j+r}$ to the corresponding summand of $\operatorname{Tot}(P_n\otimes Q_n)[r]$ by multiplication by $(-1)^{ri}$. These comparisons commute with the quotient transition maps in the reduction tower. On the product mapping-fiber model they induce the displayed isomorphism using the degreewise product shift identification and the cone comparison $\operatorname{Cone}(f[r])\to\operatorname{Cone}(f)[r]$, $(b,a)\mapsto(b,(-1)^r a)$, for the convention $\operatorname{Cone}(f)=B'\oplus A'[1]$ when $f:A'\to B'$.

source.place: Definition 3.4.10 and Lemma 3.4.12(4), pp. 22–23: completed tensor and reduction-limit construction; the explicit signed shift comparison is the agent expansion of the last sentence of literature/blueprint/main-20261015/blueprint/sec-six-functors/sk-lem-sf-twist-interchange/lem-sf-twist-interchange.proof.md.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sf-completed-tensor-finite-shift] to obtain a natural isomorphism beta of tower-valued functors. For each pair of complexes its component alpha has the required finite generator formula and already commutes with the strict transitions.

Products commute with cochain shifts. Product projections and naturality of alpha identify the two endomorphisms 1-s. Apply the mapping-cone functor to this square and compose with the inverse of Mathlib mappingCone.shiftIso. Its inr component has coefficient 1 and its inl component has coefficient (-1)^r. Both component formulas are proved from the cone injection formulas. They also prove naturality in squares of towers. Shift by -1 and use shiftFunctorComm to obtain a natural Roos comparison, with exactly the specified cone formula.

Good complexes are stable under right shifts: termwise flatness just reindexes the terms; K-flatness follows from mapBifunctorShift2Iso and the homology shift isomorphism. Independent-coefficient tensor additivity supplies that bifunctor comparison. No new resolutions are chosen.

Let epsilon be integralCompletedTensorComparison and kappa the restriction of Q.commShiftIso to good representatives in the second slot. Localize the natural Roos comparison and compose with Q.commShiftIso to obtain tau. The desired restricted isomorphism theta is kappa inverse, epsilon on shifted representatives, tau, and shifted epsilon inverse. Postcompose theta with the inverse of the output shift and compose with its unit inverse and epsilon. This makes a second descent of the same good-model functor. The uniqueness property in lem-pur-integral-operations-well-defined supplies a compatible isomorphism from the chosen descent to this one. Postcomposition with the inverse shift is fully faithful; lift the compatible isomorphism and shift unit through it. Cancellation of the descent comparisons proves that its restriction is theta, and cancellation of kappa and epsilon proves the displayed normalization on every good pair. Choose alpha from beta and the constructed cone iso as witnesses.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-N9-34684d277 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the delivery in full, recomputed every sign identity by hand and made no changes. The delivery splits the existing item into six steps and creates no new node. The statement uses the coefficient category D(W_proet,O_E)=D(B) and the completed tensor Rlim^c Res_n Tot(P_n⊗Q_n) exactly as def-pur-integral-derived-operations defines them, and does not identify it with the Bhatt–Scholze derived-completion tensor. The shift and cone conventions match def-weil-abstract-derived-category. Step 1: the Koszul sign (-1)^{ri} makes a chain map; both components (-1)^{ri+r} and (-1)^{ri+i+r} agree under the Tot convention of def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves. Step 2: Q[r] is K-flat with flat terms by step 1 and the definition in def-pc-kflat-complex, and resolutions exist by lem-pc-kflat-resolution. Step 3: the transition maps have degree 0, so the towers are isomorphic on the nose. Step 4: h_r(b,a)=(b,(-1)^r a) is a chain isomorphism; both sides equal ((-1)^r db+fa,-da), and [r][-1]=[-1][r] holds exactly. Step 5: composing steps 3 and 4 gives the map. Step 6: naturality on D(B)^2 and resolution independence follow from lem-pur-integral-operations-well-defined clauses (1) and (2), used for what they state. Test cases r=0, r=1 and a one-term complex all check out. Sources: Bhatt–Scholze Definition 3.4.10 and Lemma 3.4.12(4) on pp. 22–23, Stacks tags 011G, 012Z, 014E, 08TC, 06YS and 06YT, and the last sentence of the blueprint main-20261015 lem-sf-twist-interchange proof. No SGA is cited. No duplicate exists: the existing shift nodes are about D(O_X) or ring-level tensors. Accepted tool_uses: lem-pc-kflat-resolution and lem-pur-integral-operations-well-defined; the three cited definitions are notions, so declaring them is harmless.
